title: Conditional 2: Polite Requests and Softening with бы
titleRussian: Условное 2: Вежливые просьбы и смягчение с бы
description: The бы particle is the most common politeness device in Russian. It turns a bare request into a polite one through three frames: я хотел(а) бы, the impersonal хотелось бы, and the most polite 'не могли бы вы + infinitive.'
descriptionRussian: Частица бы — самый распространённый способ выражения вежливости в русском. Она превращает прямую просьбу в вежливую через три конструкции: я хотел(а) бы, безличное хотелось бы и самую вежливую «не могли бы вы + инфинитив».
intro: The construction from lesson 1 turns out to be how Russians are polite. A want expressed in the conditional is softer than one expressed directly, and a request phrased as a negative question is softer still, because it hands the other person an easy way to say no. None of this is about hypotheticals any more. It is about not being blunt.
rules: Я хотел / хотела / хотели бы + infinitive states your own want politely; the past form of хотеть agrees with you in gender and number.
Хотелось бы + infinitive is the impersonal version: the fixed past-neuter хотелось plus бы, with no subject and no gender agreement.
Не могли бы вы + infinitive is the most polite way to ask the listener to act; the negation makes the request easy to decline.
Each frame is one past-tense word plus бы; the structure is grammatically conditional, but the meaning is a present-time request.
The infinitive after the frame follows imperative-style aspect: perfective for one specific action (открыть, помочь), imperfective for a process (говорить).
examples: Я хотел бы кофе. (I would like a coffee.) Standard polite request for an item; хотел agrees with a masc speaker.
Я хотела бы поговорить с Леной. (I'd like to speak with Lena.) Хотела (fem) + бы + impf inf for an ongoing conversation.
Хотелось бы знать ваше мнение. (I'd like to know your opinion.) Impersonal frame; no subject expressed.
Не могли бы вы открыть окно? (Could you open the window?) Most polite request for a one-time action; pf inf открыть.
Не могли бы вы повторить вопрос? (Could you repeat the question?) The standard 'I didn't catch that' frame.
Мы хотели бы пригласить вас на ужин. (We would like to invite you to dinner.) Plural хотели + бы + pf inf for a specific invitation.

items.prompt: Если бы я _____ её адрес, я бы написал ей.
items.promptEnglish: If I had known her address, I would have written to her. (warm-up from Lesson 1)
items.hint: Recap from Lesson 1: знать is impf-only. Past masc form in the if-clause.
items.explanation: Recap from Lesson 1: знать is an impf-only state verb. Past masc form: знал. The hypothetical past + бы structure uses the same form across past, present, and future hypotheticals. Today's lesson moves to single-clause politeness uses of бы.

items.promptEnglish: I (f) would like to speak with Lena.
items.hint: Fem speaker + politeness frame for one's own want. Past fem of хотеть.
items.explanation: The 'I would like + inf' frame uses the past form of хотеть + бы. The speaker is fem, so the past form is хотела. Хочу (present) would be the bare 'I want', less polite. Хотелось is the impersonal form, which does not take a 'я' subject.

items.prompt: _____ бы знать ваше мнение по этому вопросу.
items.promptEnglish: I'd like to know your opinion on this question. (impersonal frame, no subject)
items.hint: No subject is expressed. Past-neuter impersonal form of хотеть.
items.explanation: The impersonal frame uses 'хотелось бы + inf' with no expressed subject. Past-neuter form хотелось + бы. Хочется is the present impersonal ('one wants') and does not pair with бы in this slot; хотел would require an 'я' subject; хочу would be the bare 'I want'.

items.prompt: Не могли бы вы _____ окно, пожалуйста?
items.promptEnglish: Could you open the window, please? (most polite request)
items.hint: The 'не могли бы вы + ?' structure takes a specific verb form.
items.explanation: The 'не могли бы вы + INFINITIVE' frame is the most polite request form. The infinitive открыть is the right choice. Открой / откройте would be bare imperatives (less polite); открыли would be a past form, which the вы могли бы already covers.

items.hint: Polite вы always takes the plural past form of мочь.
items.explanation: The polite вы pronoun always takes the plural past form могли + бы. Мог / могла are singular and clash with вы; можете is the present form, which the бы construction does not use. The result is a conditional politeness frame: 'were you able to + inf.'

items.prompt: Мы хотели бы _____ вас на ужин в субботу.
items.promptEnglish: We would like to invite you to dinner on Saturday.
items.hint: One specific invitation (one event, one date). Pf infinitive.
items.explanation: The invitation is one specific bounded event (one dinner, one date). The perfective infinitive пригласить is the right form after 'хотели бы.' The imperfective приглашать would frame the inviting as ongoing or repeated.

items.promptEnglish: I (m) would like to order tea, please.
items.hint: The polite want-frame for a male speaker.
items.explanation: The polite frame is past + бы: хотел бы. Хочу бы is ungrammatical (бы cannot attach to a present form); хотел был confuses бы with был.

items.promptEnglish: I (f) would like to look at the menu.
items.explanation: The frame agrees with the speaker's gender: хотела бы (feminine). Хотел бы is masculine; хочу бы is ungrammatical.

items.promptEnglish: Could you open the window? It's stuffy in here.
items.hint: The most polite request frame to a stranger.
items.explanation: The maximally polite frame is Не могли бы вы + infinitive. Dropping бы ('не могли вы') breaks the formula; 'могли бы не' would ask them NOT to do it; бы cannot attach to можете.
The frame is completed by an INFINITIVE: повторить. Повторите is an imperative, which clashes with the conditional politeness.

sentenceBuilding.answer: Я хотел бы поговорить с директором.
sentenceBuilding.translation: I (m) would like to speak with the director.
acceptableVariants: Я хотел бы поговорить с директором
sentenceBuilding.hint: Frame: я + past of хотеть + бы + infinitive.

sentenceBuilding.translation: I'd like to find out your opinion. (impersonal frame)
sentenceBuilding.hint: Impersonal frame: хотелось + бы + infinitive, no subject.

blanks: Я хотел бы _____ кофе, пожалуйста. (I (m) would like to drink a coffee, please.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: The polite request is for one specific bounded action: drinking one cup of coffee. Perfective infinitive выпить. Пить (impf inf) would frame drinking as a process or general activity, less natural for a café order.

errorCorrection.sentence: «Мы хотел бы заказать столик у окна», - сказал Антон официанту.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: 'We would like to book a table by the window,' Anton said to the waiter.
errorCorrection.explanation: The polite frame 'хотел бы + infinitive' agrees with its subject. Мы is plural, so хотели бы. Хотел is masculine singular and does not agree. Хотим ('we want') is the blunt present, which loses the softening of the conditional.

errorCorrection.sentence: Не могли бы вы закройте дверь? Здесь холодно.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Could you close the door? It's cold in here.
errorCorrection.explanation: The 'не могли бы вы + ...' frame is completed by an INFINITIVE: закрыть. Закройте is an imperative, which clashes with the polite conditional already set up by 'не могли бы вы'; you do not stack a command on top of the request frame.

errorCorrection.sentence: Я хотел бы покупать этот словарь, он очень хороший.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: I would like to buy this dictionary; it's very good.
errorCorrection.explanation: After 'хотел бы', the infinitive's aspect follows the request's meaning: a single specific purchase ('этот словарь', one dictionary) takes the perfective infinitive купить. The imperfective покупать would frame buying as a repeated or ongoing activity, which a one-item request does not fit.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: I would like coffee, please. (polite order at a café)
minimalPairs.explanation: A café order to a stranger uses the polite frame: я хотел бы. The bare 'я хочу' is grammatically fine but reads as blunt or pushy in service contexts. Adding бы to past хотел turns the request into a polite frame.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Could you open the window? (most polite frame)
minimalPairs.explanation: The most polite request form in Russian includes the negation: 'не могли бы вы + inf?'. The negation softens the ask further by offering the listener an easy 'no.' Without не the request is still polite but less deferential.

reviewVocab.term: я хотел бы / я хотела бы
reviewVocab.definition: I would like (polite frame for stating one's own desire; past form of хотеть + бы + infinitive; agrees with the speaker's gender / number)
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'Я хотел бы поговорить с вами' конструкция 'хотел бы' смягчает прямое 'хочу'.

reviewVocab.definition: I'd like (impersonal politeness frame; past-neuter form хотелось + бы + infinitive; no expressed subject; softer than 'я хотел бы')
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'Хотелось бы знать ваше мнение' нет грамматического подлежащего: говорящий остаётся в фоне.

reviewVocab.definition: could you (the most polite Russian request form; не + могли + бы + вы + infinitive; the negation offers the listener an easy decline)
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'Не могли бы вы открыть окно?' структура 'не могли бы вы + инфинитив' — самая вежливая просьба.
